free_tier.stated: 100 MB max per document; no published account-level document or storage cap ("you can continue to upload more documents ... as often as you like"). Effectively per-record 100 MB x unlimited records.

egress.terms: Not free-at-scale and not scriptable: downloads are gated by the uploader's setting and often by a Scribd subscription; there is no public direct-file URL, and pages are served as HTML viewer assets.

tooling: No working public API — the official client github.com/scribd/rscribd was archived in Oct 2019; community libs (JSCRIBD, rscribd) are dead against the current site. No rclone backend.
chaining: 100 MB/record x unlimited records is the right shape, but the chain needs a browser-driven uploader and the download side is paywalled, so it can store but not serve.
limits_note: 100 MB/file; upload requires a registered, in-good-standing account; uploader agreement grants Scribd rights to restrict access/download and to "train machine learning ... models" on content; conversion failures on large or layered PDFs.
reliability_note: Uploaded documents get converted and can fail conversion; download availability is controlled by Scribd policy, not the uploader, so retrieval can be revoked unilaterally.
confidence_note: One page read moves it to documented.
